The city of Bath was founded by the Romans almost two thousand years ago. It has been famous for its 26 pleasing architecture and healing thermal springs ever since.

There are three hot springs in Bath; one is the King's Spring, upon which the Roman Baths and a temple were 27 . The other two are the Cross Spring and the Hetling Spring, close to each other in Hot Bath Street. Although Bath is 28 known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries to make use of the 29 waters.

While the Georgians made "taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was 30 generations who paved the way, creating greater interest in Bath and its springs. Charles II , desperate for an heir and unable to produce a 31 son, came to Bath to take the waters in the hope that their magical powers would do something to 32 the situation. Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Doctor Will Skype You Now
paragraphs.translationZh: 医生现在会通过 Skype 与您联系

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Fazila is a young woman that has been dealing with eczema ( S ^ ) , a common skin condition, for the past five years, but never got it treated. The nearest hospital is an hour away, by boat and bus, and her skin condition didn't seem serious enough to make the trek, so she ignored it- until a new technology brought the doctor to her. Fazila lives on one of the remote river islands in northern Bangladesh. These islands are low-lying, temporary sand islands that are continuously formed and destroyed through sand buildup and erosion. They are home to over six million people, who face repeated displacement from flooding and erosion- which may be getting worse because of climate change-and a range of health risks, including poor nutrition, malaria (疟疾)and other water-borne diseases.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 法齐拉是一名年轻女性，过去五年一直患有湿疹（一种常见的皮肤病），却从未治疗。最近的医院要乘船、乘车一小时才能到达；她觉得病情还不至于严重到值得专程去一趟，便一直置之不理，直到一项新技术把医生带到了她身边。法齐拉住在孟加拉国北部一座偏远的河岛上。这些岛屿地势低洼，是沙子不断堆积与侵蚀形成又消失的临时沙洲。这里居住着六百多万人，他们因洪水和侵蚀而反复流离失所；气候变化可能使情况恶化。他们还面临营养不良、疟疾及其他水源性疾病等多种健康风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) The most dangerous thing for these remote island dwellers is land erosion. The second is lack of access to medical supplies and doctors. There are no doctors within miles, and while child mortality and maternal death have gone down in the rest of the country, this is not the case for the islands. The medical situation is so bad that it really takes away from the quality of their life. Yet for many island inhabitants—some of Bangladesh's poorest- paying for health care is a costly ordeal. Victims of erosion lose their houses, agricultural land and jobs as farmers, fishermen and day laborers. Though government hospitals are free, many people hesitate to go, citing long commutes, endless lines and questionable diagnoses. For convenience's sake, one-third of rural households visit unqualified village doctors, who rely on unscientific methods of treatment, according to a 2016 study in the peer-reviewed journal Global Health Action.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 对于这些偏远岛屿居民来说，最危险的事情是土地侵蚀。第二是缺乏医疗用品和医生。几英里内没有医生，虽然该国其他地区的儿童死亡率和孕产妇死亡率有所下降，但岛屿的情况并非如此。医疗状况如此糟糕，这确实降低了他们的生活质量。然而，对于许多岛屿居民（孟加拉国最贫困的一些人）来说，支付医疗费用是一场代价高昂的考验。侵蚀的受害者失去了房屋、农田以及农民、渔民和日工的工作。尽管政府医院是免费的，但许多人不愿去，理由是通勤时间长、排长队和诊断可疑。根据同行评审期刊《全球健康行动》2016 年的一项研究，三分之一的农村家庭为了方便而去看不合格的乡村医生，而乡村医生依赖不科学的治疗方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) On the islands, there9s even a colloquial (口 头的)expression for the idea of making medical care your lowest priority: It's known as “rog pushai rakha^^ in Bengali, which roughly translates to "stockpiling their diseases”- waiting to seek medical attention until a condition becomes extremely serious. Now, a new virtual medical service called Teledaktar (TD) is trying to make health care more easily accessible. Every week, TD's medical operators travel to the islands by boat, carrying a laptop, a portable printer for prescriptions and tools to run basic medical screenings such as blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature and weight. They choose an area of the island with the best Internet reception and set up a makeshift (临 时凑合的)medical center which consists of plastic stools and small tables borrowed from the locals' homes, a tent in case of rain and a sheet that is strung up to give the patients privacy during their session.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 在岛屿上，甚至有一种口语（口头的）表达将医疗保健作为最不优先考虑的想法：在孟加拉语中被称为“rog Pushai Rkha^^”，大致翻译为“储存疾病”——等待寻求医疗护理，直到病情变得极其严重。现在，一种名为 Teledaktar (TD) 的新虚拟医疗服务正在努力让医疗保健变得更容易获得。每周，TD 的医疗操作人员都会乘搭他们携带笔记本电脑、便携式处方打印机和进行血压、血糖、体温和体重等基本医疗检查的工具，选择了岛上网络信号最好的区域，并建立了一个临时医疗中心，其中包括从当地人家里借来的塑料凳子和小桌子、一个以防下雨的帐篷和一张为患者在治疗期间提供隐私的床单。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Launched in October 2018, TD has eight centers in towns and villages across rural Bangladesh and on three islands. It is funded by a nonprofit organization founded by Bangladeshi entrepreneurs, finance and technology professionals. Inside the center, the laptop screen lights up to reveal Dr. Tina Mustahid, TD's head physician, live-streamed ( 网络直播) from the capital city of Dhaka for free remote medical consultations. Affectionately called Doctor Apa一 "older sister" in Bengali- by her patients, she is one of three volunteer doctors at TD.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) TD 于 2018 年 10 月推出，在孟加拉国农村地区的城镇和村庄以及三个岛屿上设有八个中心。它由孟加拉国企业家、金融和技术专业人士创立的非营利组织资助。在中心内，笔记本电脑屏幕亮起，显示 TD 的主治医师蒂娜·穆斯塔希德 (Tina Mustahid) 医生正在从首都达卡进行免费远程医疗咨询的直播（网络直播）。阿帕医生被患者亲切地称为孟加拉语“姐姐”，她是 TD 的三名志愿医生之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) “I diagnose them through conversation,says Dr. Mustahid. '"Sometimes it's really obvious things that local doctors don't have the patience to talk through with their patients. For example, a common complaint mothers come in with is that their children refuse to eat their meals. The mothers are concerned they are dealing with indigestion, but it's because they are feeding the children packaged chips which are cheap and convenient. I tell them it is ruining their appetite and ask them to cut back on unhealthy snacks." Dr. Mustahid says building awareness about health and nutrition is important for island patients who are cut off from mainland resources.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) “我通过谈话来诊断他们，”穆斯塔希德博士说。“有时，当地医生没有耐心与患者交谈，这是非常明显的事情。例如，母亲们常见的抱怨是孩子拒绝吃饭。妈妈们担心自己会消化不良，但这是因为她们给孩子喂的是包装好的薯条，既便宜又方便。我告诉他们，这会破坏他们的食欲，并要求他们减少不健康的零食。”穆斯塔希德博士说，对于与大陆资源隔绝的岛屿患者来说，建立健康和营养意识非常重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Even off the islands, Bangladesh faces a critical deficit of health services. The country has half the doctors-per-person ratio recommended by the World Health Organization: roughly one doctor per 2,000 people, instead of one doctor per 1,000 people. And of those physicians, many are concentrated in cities: 70% of the country's population live in rural areas, yet less than 20% of health workers practice there. Over 70% of TD's 3,000 patients are female, in part because many are not comfortable speaking with local doctors who tend to be male. The rural women are mostly not literate or confident enough to travel on their own to the nearest town to visit medical facilities. Many have spent their entire lives rebuilding their homes when the islands flood. Early marriage and young motherhood, which are prevalent in these parts of Bangladesh, also contribute to the early onset of health problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 即使在岛屿之外，孟加拉国也面临着医疗服务的严重短缺。该国的人均医生比例只有世界卫生组织建议的一半：大约每2000人一名医生，而不是每1000人一名医生。这些医生中，许多集中在城市：该国 70% 的人口居住在农村地区，但只有不到 20% 的卫生工作者在农村地区执业。 TD 的 3,000 名患者中超过 70% 是女性，部分原因是许多人不愿意与当地男性医生交谈。农村妇女大多没有文化，也没有足够的信心独自前往最近的城镇看病。当岛屿洪水泛滥时，许多人一生都在重建家园。孟加拉国这些地区普遍存在早婚和年轻母亲的现象，这也是导致健康问题过早出现的原因之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) For most TD patients on the islands, Dr. Mustahid is the first big-city doctor that they've ever consulted. TD doctors are not meant to treat serious illnesses or conditions that require a doctor to be physically present, such as pregnancy. But they can write prescriptions, diagnose common ailments一including digestive issues, joint pain, skin diseases, fever and the common cold—and refer patients to doctors at local hospitals. The visit is also an opportunity for the patients, especially women, to air their concerns about aging, motherhood and reproductive health according to Dr. Mustahid. The doctors also offer health, dietary and lifestyle advice where necessary, including insight on everything from recognizing postnatal (产 后的) depression to daily exercise. Dr. Mustahid regularly recommends her patients to take a daily thirty-minute morning walk before the sun gets too intense.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 对于岛上的大多数 TD 患者来说，Mustahid 医生是他们咨询过的第一位大城市医生。 TD 医生不负责治疗需要医生亲自到场的严重疾病或病症，例如怀孕。但他们可以开处方、诊断常见疾病——包括消化问题、关节疼痛、皮肤病、发烧和普通感冒——并将患者转介给当地医院的医生。穆斯塔希德博士表示，这次访问也是患者，尤其是女性患者表达对衰老、母性和生殖健康的担忧的一个机会。医生还会在必要时提供健康、饮食和生活方式建议，包括从识别产后抑郁症到日常锻炼等各个方面的见解。穆斯塔希德医生经常建议她的病人在阳光变得太强烈之前每天早上散步三十分钟。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) After a few sessions about general health issues Fazila finally opened up about something else that was bothering her: her persistent skin condition. It can get expensive to travel to the doctor, so usually the women living on the islands describe their illness to their husbands. The husbands then go to the pharmacy, try to describe the issue and return home with some random medicines. Nothing worked for Fazila until she started seeing Dr. Apa.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 在几次关于一般健康问题的会议之后，法齐拉终于谈到了困扰她的其他事情：她持续的皮肤状况。去看医生的费用可能会很高，因此生活在岛上的妇女通常会向丈夫描述她们的病情。然后，丈夫们去药房，尝试描述问题，然后随机带一些药物回家。在法齐拉开始见阿帕医生之前，一切都不起作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Other nonprofits are also starting to provide health services on the islands. A local non-governmental organization called Friendship operates floating boat hospitals that provide health services to islands all over Bangladesh, docking at each for two months at a time. Friendship also runs satellite clinics in which one doctor and one clinic aide who are residents of the community disperse health and hygiene information.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 其他非营利组织也开始在岛上提供医疗服务。当地一个名为“友谊”的非政府组织经营着浮动船医院，为孟加拉国各地的岛屿提供医疗服务，每个医院每次停靠两个月。友谊还经营卫星诊所，其中一名医生和一名诊所助理都是社区居民，负责传播健康和卫生信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) TD still has a few major challenges. Many residents complain the medicines they are prescribed are sometimes unaffordable, but the government isn't doing enough for them. Patients often ask why the medicine isn't free along with the consultation from the doctors. The organizations are linked to local pharmacies and offer discounts to the patients and make sure to prescribe the most cost-effective brands, but still many residents can't afford even that.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) TD 仍然面临一些重大挑战。许多居民抱怨他们开的药有时买不起，但政府为他们做的还不够。在医生的咨询下，患者常常会问为什么药不是免费的。这些组织与当地药店有联系，为患者提供折扣，并确保开出最具成本效益的品牌处方，但许多居民仍然买不起。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Nevertheless, TD's remote consultations seem to be popular: Of 3,000 patients, at least 200 have returned for follow-ups, according to TD. The reason, explains one resident, might be the simple gesture of treating the island inhabitants with respect. ctDr. Apa is patient,“ he says, “At government hospitals, the doctors treat us very badly, but here they listen to us, I can repeat myself many times and no one gets annoyed.^^
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 尽管如此，TD 的远程咨询似乎很受欢迎：据 TD 称，在 3,000 名患者中，至少有 200 人返回进行随访。一位居民解释说，原因可能是尊重岛上居民的简单姿态。 ct博士。 Apa很有耐心，”他说，“在政府医院，医生对我们的态度很不好，但在这里他们会听我们的话，我可以重复很多遍，没有人会生气。^^

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Some children on the remote islands won't eat their meals because they are fed cheap junk food.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 偏远岛屿上的一些儿童不吃饭，因为他们吃的是廉价垃圾食品。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Unlike other parts of Bangladesh, the number of women who die from giving birth remains high on the river islands.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 与孟加拉国其他地区不同，河流岛屿上死于分娩的妇女人数仍然很高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. One big problem many islanders have is that they can't afford the prescribed medicines, even with discounts offered.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 许多岛民面临的一大问题是，即使有折扣，他们也买不起处方药。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. TD is a virtual medical service financially supported by one of the nation's nonprofit organizations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. TD 是一项虚拟医疗服务，由国家非营利组织之一提供资金支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. TD doctors are welcome to the islanders because they treat the sick with respect and patience.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. TD医生受到岛民的欢迎，因为他们以尊重和耐心的态度对待病人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Women islanders tend to have health problems early partly because they get married and give birth early.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 岛民女性往往较早出现健康问题，部分原因是她们结婚和生育较早。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. TD doctors make weekly visits to the remote islands to provide services at a temporary medical center.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. TD医生每周前往偏远岛屿，在临时医疗中心提供服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. TD doctors provide the islanders with online diagnoses and treatments for common diseases.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. TD医生为岛民提供常见疾病的在线诊断和治疗。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The residents of the river islands have to keep moving their homes because of floods and land erosions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 由于洪水和土地侵蚀，河上岛屿的居民不得不不断搬迁家园。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Women islanders usually rely on their husbands to get some medicines for them without diagnoses and prescriptions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 岛民中的女性通常依靠丈夫在没有诊断和处方的情况下为她们获取一些药物。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive, and for not training graduates for the world of work. Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国的一些精英学院和大学因过于精英化、学费过高以及不培养适合职场的毕业生而受到批评。这些指控忽视了这样一个事实：这些机构继续帮助学生为工作成功、深思熟虑地参与公民生活、终身学习以及了解世界和与他们一起生活的人做好准备。

paragraphs.sourceText: These colleges and universities must be doing something right. Applications are at record highs, and their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever. This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些学院和大学必须做正确的事情。申请数量创下历史新高，他们的经济援助计划使申请比以往任何时候都更容易。这种教育模式长期以来在创造机会、推动经济增长和刺激创新方面发挥着核心作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yet, there is growing skepticism about the value of this model. The recent tax reform bill is a wake-up call that our strongest colleges and universities are under assault by some in government. The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest. Thankfully, these provisions were ultimately stripped from the bill, but lawmakers let stand a new tax on the investment income of some colleges and universities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，人们越来越怀疑这种模式的价值。最近的税收改革法案敲响了警钟：我们最强大的学院和大学正受到政府中一些人的攻击。最初的提议将对研究生征收学费减免税并终止学生贷款利息的扣除，从而使许多人无法承担教育费用。值得庆幸的是，这些条款最终被从法案中删除，但立法者允许对一些学院和大学的投资收入征收新税。

paragraphs.sourceText: While these attacks are motivated by misguided ideas, we need to do a better job of explaining why these claims are false and why what we do is valuable. We cannot take for granted that any of this is obvious.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然这些攻击是由误导性想法引发的，但我们需要更好地解释为什么这些说法是错误的以及为什么我们所做的事情是有价值的。我们不能想当然地认为这些都是显而易见的。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is often said that elite colleges and universities do not train students, particularly those who study the liberal arts, for the workforce. But this can be refuted by scholarly research. The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work. This education develops the skills of critical thinking, rigorous analysis of data and facts, communication with the written and spoken word, understanding of cultural differences and issues, and the ability to keep learning. In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们常说，精英学院和大学并不为劳动力培养学生，特别是那些学习文科的学生。但这可以通过学术研究反驳。数据很清楚：文科教育是很好的职业准备，既可以为你带来丰厚的终生收入，也可以让你对工作感到满意。这种教育培养批判性思维、对数据和事实进行严格分析、书面和口头交流的技能、对文化差异和问题的理解以及持续学习的能力。事实上，文科毕业生在每个可以想象的领域都表现得非常好。

paragraphs.sourceText: Access to an education at selective colleges and universities is now more available than ever to low-and middle-income families. We have built endowments from donations by alumni (校友)and parents who understand and appreciate our mission to provide access and opportunity, and a significant portion of the returns from these endowments is used to fund financial aid.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，低收入和中等收入家庭比以往任何时候都更有机会在选择性学院和大学接受教育。我们通过校友和家长的捐赠建立了捐赠基金，他们理解并欣赏我们提供机会和机会的使命，这些捐赠的回报的很大一部分用于资助经济援助。

paragraphs.sourceText: Ironically, the new tax on endowments drains financial aid funds from the very schools most able to offer opportunity to those who have earned a spot but cannot otherwise afford this education. Beyond the virtue of access to those who have earned a place at these schools, the diversity of economic backgrounds enhances the education and experience of all of our students.
paragraphs.translationZh: 具有讽刺意味的是，新的捐赠税耗尽了最有能力为那些已获得学位但无法负担教育费用的学生提供机会的学校的经济援助资金。除了能够接触到在这些学校获得一席之地的学生之外，经济背景的多样性也增强了我们所有学生的教育和经验。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: When a group of Australians was asked why they believed climate change was not happening, about 36% said it was “common sense”, according to a report published last year by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organization. This was the most popular reason fbr their opinion, with only 11% saying their belief that climate change was not happening was based on scientific research.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据联邦科学与工业研究组织去年发布的一份报告，当一群澳大利亚人被问及为什么他们认为气候变化没有发生时，大约 36% 的人表示这是“常识”。这是他们观点中最常见的原因，只有 11% 的人表示他们认为气候变化没有发生的信念是基于科学研究。

paragraphs.sourceText: But what do we mean by an appeal to common sense? Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning. The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right, but what feels right to one person may not feel right to another. Whether it feels right is usually a reflection of the world view and ideologies we have internalised, and that frames how we interact with new ideas. When new ideas are in accord with what we already believe, they are more readily accepted. When they are not, they, and the arguments that lead to them, are more readily rejected.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但我们所说的诉诸常识是什么意思呢？据推测，这是对某种理性的诉求，构成了更复杂推理的基础。然而，诉诸常识通常只不过是诉诸感觉正确的想法，但一个人感觉正确的事情可能对其他人来说并不感觉正确。感觉是否正确通常反映了我们内化的世界观和意识形态，并决定了我们如何与新想法互动。当新的想法与我们已经相信的一致时，它们更容易被接受。如果不是，那么它们以及导致它们的论点就更容易被拒绝。

paragraphs.sourceText: We often mistake this automatic compatibility testing of new ideas with existing beliefs as an application of common sense, but, in reality, it is more about judging than thinking. As Nobelist Daniel Kahneman notes in Thinking, Fast and Slow, when we arrive at conclusions in this way, the outcomes also feel true, regardless of whether they are. We are not psychologically well equipped to judge our own thinking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们经常将这种新想法与现有信念的自动兼容性测试误认为是常识的应用，但实际上，它更多的是判断而不是思考。正如诺贝尔奖获得者丹尼尔·卡尼曼在《思考，快与慢》中指出的那样，当我们以这种方式得出结论时，结果也会感觉是真实的，无论它们是否真实。我们在心理上没有能力判断自己的想法。

paragraphs.sourceText: We are also highly susceptible to a range of cognitive biases such as giving preference to the first things that come to mind when making decisions or giving weight to evidence.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们也很容易受到一系列认知偏见的影响，例如在做出决定时优先考虑首先想到的事情或重视证据。

paragraphs.sourceText: One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people. The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们检查内部偏见和不一致的方法之一是通过知识的社会验证，以严格和系统的方式测试我们的想法，看看它们是否不仅对我们有意义，对其他人也有意义。这种社会共享认知的突出例子是科学。

paragraphs.sourceText: That does not mean that individuals are not capable of excellent thinking, nor does it mean no individual is rational. But the extent to which individuals can do this on their own is a function of how well integrated they are with communities of systematic inquiry in the first place. You can't learn to think well by yourself.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这并不意味着个人没有出色的思考能力，也不意味着没有个人是理性的。但个人能够在多大程度上自己做到这一点首先取决于他们与系统探究社区的融合程度。你无法靠自己学会好好思考。

paragraphs.sourceText: In matters of science at least, those who value their common sense over methodological, collaborative investigation imagine themselves to be more free in their thinking, unbound by involvement with the group, but in reality they are tightly bound by their capabilities and perspectives. We are smarter together than we are individually, and perhaps that's just common sense.
paragraphs.translationZh: 至少在科学问题上，那些重视常识胜过方法论、协作研究的人想象自己的思维更加自由，不受团体参与的束缚，但实际上他们受到自己的能力和观点的严格束缚。我们在一起比单独行动更聪明，也许这只是常识。
